claims.text: In the early sixth century, Aksumite intervention defeated the Himyarite regime and established control over large parts of southwest Arabia.
The Sasanians intervened militarily in Yemen around 570 and displaced Aksumite power.
Later Arabic chronicles associate Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan with seeking outside help and with the Sasanian intervention; details and sequencing vary.
Sirat Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan is a late-medieval Egyptian popular epic that rewrites its historical setting and includes jinn, enchanted objects, and the diversion of the Nile.

Himyar ruled from Zafar in the fifth and early sixth centuries and its surviving material culture includes monumental architecture, inscriptions, stone sculpture, and metalwork shaped by broad trade contacts.
